one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban chronicles the first major party-list challenge -- who can qualify -- by tracing the jurisprudential arc from Ang Bagong Bayani v. Comelec (June 26, 2001, which he wrote for a 9-5 majority) through Banat (2009) and Atong Paglaum (April 2, 2013). Ang Bagong Bayani held that only parties and nominees belonging to the 'marginalized and underrepresented' were eligible -- so that Payatas hovel dwellers, not Forbes Park mansion owners, would become veritable lawmakers. Banat further excluded major parties already well-represented in district polls. But Atong Paglaum reversed these rulings, allowing national and regional parties without any marginalized constituency to join the party-list as long as their members advocate common ideologies -- interpreting 'marginalized and underrepresented' primarily in the electoral sense. CJ discloses he 'fought valiantly' in Ang Bagong Bayani, that CJ Puno barely blocked major parties in Banat by an 8-7 vote, and CJ Sereno's dissent in Atong Paglaum was 'snowed down by an avalanche of votes.' He notes that as early as 2001 he urged Congress to craft a clearer law, but the beneficiaries failed to act, and now only a constitutional convention -- not a constituent assembly -- may offer a remedy.
